settings.eyebrow: Rooftop cafe & espresso bar · Seventh floor of the Meridian Building
settings.headline:
Coffee and sky,
a storey above the city.
settings.copy: The Gilded Terrace is a rooftop cafe perched above the city's west end — small-batch coffee, light seasonal plates, and slow evenings under string lights with a skyline view you can't get anywhere else.

trust_list.text: Small-batch beans roasted weekly, thirty miles away
Seventh-floor skyline view, open-air in the warm months
Seasonal plates built around what's in season
Quiet enough to work, warm enough to linger

stats.label: Storeys up — the city's only rooftop cafe
Seats with a direct view of the skyline
From the roastery that supplies our beans

settings.title: What's
settings.intro: A small, rotating menu built for a rooftop. Coffee changes with the roaster's weekly drop; the kitchen follows the season and the sky.

items.name: Golden Hour Cortado
items.description: Double shot pulled tight over velvet micro-foam, finished with a pinch of smoked sea salt and a whisper of honey. Our signature.

items.name: Skyline Cold Brew
items.description: Eighteen-hour slow-steeped, served over a single large cube with a twist of orange. Clean, bright, and bracingly cold.

items.name: Rooftop Matcha
items.description: Ceremonial-grade matcha whisked to order with oat milk and a touch of maple. Green, grassy, and gently sweet.

items.name: Dusk Flat White
items.description: A double ristretto with silky full-cream milk — the drink the regulars order as the sun drops below the skyline.

items.name: Heirloom Tomato Toast
items.description: Sourdough, whipped ricotta, blistered heirloom tomatoes, and a drizzle of basil oil. The reason people stay past their coffee.

items.name: Honey-Burnt Fig Plate
items.description: Roasted figs, whipped goat cheese, candied walnuts, and warm honey over toast. Dessert that thinks it's breakfast.

settings.title: More than
settings.intro: Good coffee is table stakes. What keeps people coming back to the roof is the combination — the view, the pace, and the little details that make a cafe feel like a place, not a stop.

features.title: A skyline that does the work
features.text: West-facing tables catch the full golden hour, and the open-air terrace means you watch the city lights come on as you finish your coffee.

features.title: Beans from thirty miles away
features.text: We roast with a small local roastery on a weekly schedule, so the coffee is never more than a week off the roaster. You can taste the difference.

features.title: A kitchen that follows the season
features.text: The menu changes with the farmers market. Tomatoes in summer, figs in fall, citrus in winter — a small board that never gets boring.

features.title: Quiet enough to actually work
features.text: Weekday mornings are a working cafe: reliable wifi, low music, and outlets at half the tables. It's a rooftop office for people who like light.

features.title: Evenings made for lingering
features.text: After six the lights go warm and the pace slows. It's a place for a second coffee, a shared plate, and conversation that runs long.

features.title: A team that knows your order
features.text: The baristas remember faces and regulars, pour with intention, and will happily talk beans or the view for as long as you like.

settings.intro: A glimpse of the roof in different lights — dawn espresso, golden-hour glow, and the blue of a city evening.

settings.title: The roof
settings.intro: People don't just pass through the Gilded Terrace — they develop habits around it. Here's what the regulars say.

reviews.quote: I work here three mornings a week. There's no better place to start the day than a flat white with the whole city waking up below you. The staff know my order and my name.
reviews.author: Mara Chen

reviews.quote: The golden hour here is genuinely unmatched. We came for the view and stayed for the cortado — and the fig plate. Now it's our Friday ritual.
reviews.author: Jonas & Priya

reviews.quote: I've tried every coffee shop downtown and this is the one I keep returning to. It's the combination — the light, the quiet, the beans. Nothing else comes close.
reviews.author: Sam Okafor

settings.title: Come up
settings.intro: Take the lift to the seventh floor of the Meridian Building. Come for the coffee, stay for the sky — and bring a book, a laptop, or a friend.
